title: Intelligence Security Laboratories — Room 452, a small glass-front office; MDL 6060 E ENV quoted
anchor: client email 14 Sep (widths 65" / 67", length 100" at its longest, 96" to the door handle, door 36", ceiling 90" lowest / 114" over the first third). Supersedes the booth-builder room fields (100 x 65 x 7'6", link 187bf0c5c898). Where the 67" third sits and the door's jamb offset are read off the photos and assumed.
interpretations: The five inputs are room PHOTOS with no measurements. All stated numbers come from the client's email of 14 Sep, which supersedes the booth-builder room fields sales typed (100" x 65" x 7'6"). The email does not say WHICH third is 67" wide, on which side, or where the ceiling steps; those are read off the photos and recorded as assumed.

Which way the 100" and 65" run: the glass front (door + sidelight) is the SHORT wall. IMG_3801/3802, from the doorway, look down a deep narrow room; IMG_3805, from inside, shows the front wall as one 36" door leaf plus a sidelight about 21" wide. So 65"/67" is across the room and 100" runs away from the door.

Orientation is arbitrary (photos carry no north): the glass front is drawn as the SOUTH wall and the back wall NORTH. From inside looking out (IMG_3805) the door is at the left end of the front wall, so the solid hinge-side wall is EAST and the desk / glass-return side is WEST.

The 67" third: placed at the FRONT (south) end, with the 2" step in the WEST wall. At the SW corner the glass partition turns and runs north along the west wall before the wall becomes drywall (IMG_3804, IMG_3805). In IMG_3801 the glass-to-drywall junction shows a black end member facing the doorway, which reads as the drywall standing proud of the glass plane; so the room is wider along the glass return. It is also the same 'first third' as the client's 114" ceiling, where IMG_3802 shows open deck above the doorway before the suspended cloud begins. The east wall shows no step in any photo.

Door swing: INTO the room, as the client's email implies ('not being able to open the door all the way to get in') and the photos show: IMG_3805 (inside) has the hinge knuckles on the east jamb, and IMG_3801 shows the leaf standing open inside the room.

Ceiling: built at the client's LOWEST figure, 90", because a take-off room carries one ceiling. The client's 114" over 'the first third' is the open-deck zone at the door end; its edge is put at the same assumed 33" line as the width jump, 67" from the back wall. Overhead in the 90" zone: a suspended white cloud with a linear pendant light hung below it (IMG_3801/3802). Whether the pendant hangs below 90" is not known.
Client furniture (desk, chair, bin along the west wall) is not modelled.

notes: Room 452 (number on the frame, IMG_3804). Glass front faces the corridor.
Client email 14 Sep supersedes the booth-builder fields (100 x 65 x 7'6"). The client also says: 'If we cannot switch to a sliding door this is reduced.' A sliding door gives the full 96-100" back.
The door swings IN. The client measured an 18" opening as enough to enter, and gives 'max length approx 78"' for the booth with the door used that way.
Glass sidelight between the door frame and the SW corner is roughly 21-23" by the photo scale; the glass returns north along the west wall for about the first third (assumed to be the 67" part).

Ceiling: 90" lowest (built), 114" over the first third at the door end (not built; edge assumed at 67" from the back wall). Overhead in the 90" zone: a suspended cloud and a linear pendant light hung below it. The pendant's drop is unknown.
Client furniture not modelled: desk, chair, bin along the west wall.
